ei.title: 특이한 것을 이해하기 위한 평범한 것에 대한 이해의 필요성

fullPassage: It is much more natural to be surprised by unusual phenomena like eclipses than ordinary phenomena like falling bodies or the succession of night into day and day into night. Many cultures invented gods to explain these eclipses that shocked, frightened, or surprised them; but very few imagined a god of falling bodies ― to which they were so accustomed that they did not even notice them. But the reason for eclipses is ultimately the same as that of the succession of night and day: the movement of celestial bodies, which itself is based on the Newtonian law of attraction and how it explains why things fall when we let them go. For the physicist, understanding the ordinary, the habitual, and the frequent thus allows us to account for the frightening and the singular. As such, it was thus necessary to ask "Why do things fall?" and to have Newton's response to understand a broad range of much more bizarre phenomena occurring at every level of the universe.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

It is much more natural to be surprised by unusual phenomena like eclipses than ordinary phenomena like falling bodies or the succession of night into day and day into night.

(A) But the reason for eclipses is ultimately the same as that of the succession of night and day: the movement of celestial bodies, which itself is based on the Newtonian law of attraction and how it explains why things fall when we let them go.
(B) Many cultures invented gods to explain these eclipses that shocked, frightened, or surprised them; but very few imagined a god of falling bodies ― to which they were so accustomed that they did not even notice them.
(C) For the physicist, understanding the ordinary, the habitual, and the frequent thus allows us to account for the frightening and the singular.

det.analysis:
✅ ② (B)-(A)-(C): (B) 문화들이 일식에 신을 만들었지만 낙하체는 익숙 → (A) 일식의 이유는 밤낮과 같으며 뉴턴 법칙 → (C) 물리학자에게 평범한 것의 이해가 핵심
❌ ① (A)부터 시작하면 'But the reason'의 But이 S1과 직접 연결이 어색
❌ ③ (C)부터 시작하면 물리학자 관점이 맥락 없이 등장
❌ ④ (B)-(C)-(A)이면 C의 결론 후 A의 설명이 역순
det.tip: But(역접) → S1에서 놀라움 언급 후 (B)에서 신/익숙함 대비 → (A) 이유 설명 → (C) 결론

questions.stem:

Many cultures invented gods to explain these eclipses that shocked, frightened, or surprised them; but very few imagined a god of falling bodies ― to which they were so accustomed that they did not even notice them.

(A) As such, it was thus necessary to ask "Why do things fall?" and to have Newton's response to understand a broad range of much more bizarre phenomena occurring at every level of the universe.
(B) For the physicist, understanding the ordinary, the habitual, and the frequent thus allows us to account for the frightening and the singular.
(C) But the reason for eclipses is ultimately the same as that of the succession of night and day: the movement of celestial bodies, which itself is based on the Newtonian law of attraction and how it explains why things fall when we let them go.

det.analysis:
✅ ④ (C)-(B)-(A): (C) 일식의 이유=천체 운동+뉴턴 법칙 → (B) 물리학자에게 평범한 것 이해→무서운 것 설명 → (A) As such(그러므로) 질문과 뉴턴 응답으로 넓은 현상 이해
❌ ① (A)의 'As such'는 결론이므로 먼저 올 수 없음
❌ ② (B) 다음에 (C) 이유가 오면 역순
❌ ③ (C)→(A)이면 'As such'가 (B)의 결론 없이 나옴
det.tip: As such = 그러므로 — 결론 표지어, 마지막에 위치

questions.stem: 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? However, the underlying cause of these spectacular events is far simpler than it appears.

det.analysis:
❌ ① S1 뒤: 아직 원인이 언급되지 않아 'underlying cause'가 갑작스러움
✅ ② S2 뒤: 신을 만들고 익숙함을 언급한 후, 'However 실제 원인은 훨씬 간단'이라는 전환이 자연스럽고 S3의 과학적 설명으로 연결
❌ ③ S3 뒤: 이미 원인을 설명한 후이므로 '원인이 간단하다'는 말이 중복
❌ ④ S4 뒤: 물리학자 관점 정리 후이므로 맥락에 맞지 않음
det.tip: However = 그러나 — 앞(신화적 설명)과 뒤(과학적 설명)를 연결하는 전환어

questions.passage: It is much more natural to be surprised by unusual phenomena like eclipses than ordinary phenomena like ____ (falling)______ bodies or the succession of night into day and day into night. Many cultures invented gods to explain these eclipses that shocked, frightened, or surprised them; but very few imagined a god of falling bodies ― to which they were so accustomed that they did not even notice them. But the reason for eclipses is ultimately the same as that of the succession of night and day: the movement of celestial bodies, which itself is based on the Newtonian law of attraction and how it explains why things fall when we let them go. For the physicist, understanding the ordinary, the habitual, and the frequent thus allows us to account for the frightening and the singular.
